title: Then Māra approached the Blessed One; having approached, he spoke this verse to the Blessed One: Why are you still sleeping, Why are you still…
content:
Then Māra approached the Blessed One; having approached, he spoke this verse to the Blessed One:
Why are you still sleeping,
Why are you still sleeping,
Why do you sleep like this,
Like a dead man curled up?
Thinking the house is empty,
Thus you sleep,
Why do you sleep like this
When the sun has risen?

( Blessed One ):
When there is no craving,
With its net and poison,
One thus freed
Is not led anywhere.
Māra! The Enlightened One,
All attachments destroyed,
If he sleeps,
What can you do?

title: Bhikkhus, while I dwelt heedful, ardent, and resolute, when a thought of renunciation arose, I understood: 'This thought of renunciation has arisen in me, and…
content: Bhikkhus, while I dwelt heedful, ardent, and resolute, when a thought of renunciation arose, I understood: 'This thought of renunciation has arisen in me, and it does not lead to my own harm, nor to others' harm, nor to the harm of both, it increases wisdom, is not associated with distress, and leads to Nibbāna.' Bhikkhus, if I reflected and pondered upon it at night, I saw no danger from that cause. If I reflected and pondered upon it by day, I saw no danger from that cause. If I reflected and pondered upon it night and day, I saw no danger from that cause. But if I reflected and pondered upon it for too long, my body would become fatigued; when the body is fatigued, the mind becomes agitated; when the mind is agitated, it is far from concentration. Bhikkhus, I then internally steadied my mind, settled it, unified it, and concentrated it. Why is that? So that my mind would not be agitated.

title: Headman, the Sakyan samaṇas are not permitted to use gold and silver. The Sakyan samaṇas do not accept gold and silver. The Sakyan samaṇas do…
content: Headman, the Sakyan samaṇas are not permitted to use gold and silver. The Sakyan samaṇas do not accept gold and silver. The Sakyan samaṇas do not receive gold and silver. The Sakyan samaṇas have abandoned gems and gold and silver. They have renounced gold and silver. For one who is permitted to use gold and silver, that person is also permitted to use the five strands of sensual pleasure. For one who is permitted to use the five strands of sensual pleasure, that person completely upholds what is not the samaṇa's practice, not the Sakyan's practice. Headman, I say this: Grass is to be sought by one who needs grass. Wood is to be sought by one who needs wood. A vehicle is to be sought by one who needs a vehicle. A person is to be sought by one who needs a person. But for no reason whatsoever, headman, do I say that gold and silver are to be accepted, are to be sought.

title: ( Yakkha ): Greed and hatred, From what cause do they arise? Discontent and contentment, Fear, from where do they arise? From where do there…
content:
( Yakkha ):
Greed and hatred,
From what cause do they arise?
Discontent and contentment,
Fear, from where do they arise?
From where do there arise
Thoughts and reflections,
Like crows that children
Let fly and then pull back?

( Blessed One ):
Greed and hatred
Arise from this cause,
Discontent and contentment,
Fear arise from here.
From here there arise
Thoughts and reflections,
Like crows that children
Let fly and then pull back.
They arise from craving,
They arise from self.
Like a banyan tree
Grows from its own trunk.
Ordinary people cling to evil desires,
Like creepers spreading through the forest.
Those who understand
That from this cause they arise,
Destroy that cause.
Listen, yakkha,
They cross this flood,
The flood so hard to cross,
Never crossed before,
Without being reborn again.

title: 'Venerable Nun, in pleasant feeling, what underlying tendency (anusaya) persists? In painful feeling, what underlying tendency persists? In neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, what underlying tendency persists?' —…
content: 'Venerable Nun, in pleasant feeling, what underlying tendency (anusaya) persists? In painful feeling, what underlying tendency persists? In neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, what underlying tendency persists?' — 'Friend Visākha, in pleasant feeling, the underlying tendency to lust persists; in painful feeling, the underlying tendency to aversion persists; in neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, the underlying tendency to ignorance persists.' — 'Venerable Nun, does the underlying tendency to lust persist in all pleasant feeling? Does the underlying tendency to aversion persist in all painful feeling? Does the underlying tendency to ignorance persist in all neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling?' — 'Friend Visākha, it is not that the underlying tendency to lust persists in all pleasant feeling, nor that the underlying tendency to aversion persists in all painful feeling, nor that the underlying tendency to ignorance persists in all neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.' — 'Venerable Nun, in pleasant feeling, what should be abandoned? In painful feeling, what should be abandoned? In neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, what should be abandoned?' — 'Friend Visākha, in pleasant feeling, the underlying tendency to lust should be abandoned; in painful feeling, the underlying tendency to aversion should be abandoned; in neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, the underlying tendency to ignorance should be abandoned.' — 'Venerable Nun, should the underlying tendency to lust be abandoned in all pleasant feeling? Should the underlying tendency to aversion be abandoned in all painful feeling? Should the underlying tendency to ignorance be abandoned in all neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling?' — 'Friend Visākha, it is not that the underlying tendency to lust should be abandoned in all pleasant feeling, nor that the underlying tendency to aversion should be abandoned in all painful feeling, nor that the underlying tendency to ignorance should be abandoned in all neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.'

title: Whatever kind of conditioned phenomena, bhikkhus, the Noble Eightfold Path is declared the foremost among them. Those who have confidence in the Noble Eightfold Path…
content: Whatever kind of conditioned phenomena, bhikkhus, the Noble Eightfold Path is declared the foremost among them. Those who have confidence in the Noble Eightfold Path have confidence in the foremost. For those who have confidence in the foremost, the result is foremost.

title: Here, Mallikā, a certain woman is not irritable and not very malicious; even when spoken to much, she does not become exasperated, angry, hostile, aggressive,…
content: Here, Mallikā, a certain woman is not irritable and not very malicious; even when spoken to much, she does not become exasperated, angry, hostile, aggressive, provocative, does not display irritation, hatred, or displeasure. She gives to ascetics and brahmins food, drink, clothing, vehicles, garlands, scents, ointments, beds, dwellings, lamps; she is not stingy; seeing others receiving gain, honor, respect, reverence, homage, offerings, she does not envy, resent, or become bound by envy. That woman, after leaving this life, returning to this state, is reborn with beautiful complexion, good appearance, serene, possessing excellent form, wealthy, with great property, great possessions, great influence.

title: A giver, Sīha, a donor, whatever assembly he approaches — whether an assembly of nobles, brahmins, householders, or ascetics — he approaches with confidence, without…
content: A giver, Sīha, a donor, whatever assembly he approaches — whether an assembly of nobles, brahmins, householders, or ascetics — he approaches with confidence, without hesitation or perplexity. This, Sīha, is a directly visible benefit of giving.

title: Elder Vāraṇa: Whoever among people harms other beings, That person harms himself in this life and the next. But one with a compassionate heart, pitying…
content:
Elder Vāraṇa:

Whoever among people harms other beings,
That person harms himself in this life and the next.

But one with a compassionate heart, pitying all beings,
A person acting thus reaps abundant merit.

Learn to speak well, serve the ascetics,
Live alone secluded, with a peaceful mind.

title: The thoughts of craving Are a person's sensual pleasures, The beautiful things in the world Are not the sensual pleasures, The thoughts of craving Are…
content:
The thoughts of craving
Are a person's sensual pleasures,
The beautiful things in the world
Are not the sensual pleasures,
The thoughts of craving
Are a person's sensual pleasures,
The beautiful things remain
As they are in the world,
But the wise
Subdue desire for them.
